finding.claim: Unvalidated profile icon URL is stored and later fetched server-side by the nightly sync job, giving blind second-order SSRF to arbitrary internal or metadata endpoints.
finding.source: icon parameter of update(String webhook, String icon) (src/Profile.java:11), exposed via PUT /profile per the comment at :10
finding.sink: c.send(HttpRequest GET to URI.create(iconUrl)) in sync() (src/Profile.java:23-24)

trace.note: this.iconUrl = icon stored with no validation
sync() nightly job, uses HttpClient c with server network position
GET issued and body read into byte array; response discarded, so blind

finding.guards_checked: update() only validates webhook (line 12-14); icon has no scheme, host, port, allowlist, or null check; sync() performs no re-validation before the request. java.net.http limits schemes to http/https. Unknown: injected HttpClient c redirect policy (not in repo); if it follows redirects, a public host could redirect into internal space.

verdict.reason: The trace lines are accurate: src/Profile.java:16 stores icon unvalidated, and the sink at :23-24 calls URI.create(iconUrl) and sends a GET. No guard closes it, since the only check (:12-14) covers webhook. The source is not confirmed as attacker-controllable: the only evidence is the comment "PUT /profile" at :10, and no route, handler, or auth config exists in the repo (grep found no other references to update(), PUT, or /profile). Whether an unauthenticated or low-privilege caller can reach update() therefore cannot be decided from this code, and the injected HttpClient's redirect policy is also unknown.
